title: Microsoft Teams: tenant meeting policy for who can start recording and transcription
summary: The briefing accurately separates the planned tenant policy from existing recording controls, and its status, target and availability match the roadmap. The documented controls are supported; the sensitivity-label path should include the scope-selection page already explained in its note.

claims.claim: This roadmap item concerns Microsoft Teams.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Teams"]

claims.claim: Microsoft plans meeting-policy controls over who can start recording.
claims.quote: Teams administrators can use meeting policies to control who can start recording and transcription, helping organizations apply consistent meeting settings.

claims.claim: The planned meeting policy also controls who can start transcription.
claims.quote: Teams administrators can use meeting policies to control who can start recording and transcription

claims.claim: The planned policy can restrict these permissions to organisers and co-organisers.
claims.quote: Administrators can restrict these permissions to organizers and co-organizers or extend them to presenters.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope
claims.claim: The planned policy can extend the permissions to presenters.
claims.quote: Administrators can restrict these permissions to organizers and co-organizers or extend them to presenters.

claims.claim: Administrators will be able to allow organiser changes or enforce the planned setting.
claims.quote: They can also determine whether meeting organizers can modify these settings or whether they are enforced by policy.

claims.where: controls[0].ui and controls[0].api; summary; What's changing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn does not yet document the planned tenant policy, its admin-centre path or its PowerShell parameter.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams tenant who can record transcribe meeting policy 579860 default license PowerShell; Teams tenant who can record meeting policy admin center PowerShell default. Opened meeting-recording, manage-meeting-recording-options and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; no matching policy or parameter.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Scope; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The planned control's default is not stated, so defaultState is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams tenant who can record meeting policy admin center PowerShell default. Read the roadmap, meeting-recording, manage-meeting-recording-options and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; none states the planned control's initial enforcement or default.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing and price for the new tenant policy are not yet published, and the roadmap names neither.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams 579860 licensing price administrator role; Teams Who can record policy license tenant. Read roadmap, meeting-recording and manage-meeting-recording-options; licensing-enhance-teams search excerpts concern existing organiser features, not the planned tenant policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a configuring role specifically for the new policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams 579860 licensing price administrator role. Read roadmap and meeting-recording; results included general Teams Administrator permissions, but no role requirement specific to the planned policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn has not documented how the new tenant policy relates to meeting sensitivity, labels or templates.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams tenant policy record transcribe sensitivity labels default licensing. Read manage-meeting-recording-options, meeting-templates-sensitivity-labels-policies and sensitivity-labels-meetings; they cover existing controls, not the new policy's interactions.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity and Change & support
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented how the new policy combines with the existing recording and transcription policies.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams tenant who can record transcribe meeting policy 579860 default license PowerShell. Read meeting-recording, meeting-transcription-captions and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; no interaction with the planned role-restriction policy is described.

claims.claim: Neither the roadmap nor the researched Learn documentation announces a change to existing behaviour if administrators do nothing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams tenant who can record meeting policy admin center PowerShell default. Read roadmap, meeting-recording and manage-meeting-recording-options; no automatic change to existing permissions is stated. Continuing today's behaviour is explicitly the briefing's rating assumption.

claims.claim: No Message Center post for this item was available in the supplied evidence.
claims.quote: Searched: 579860 Message center. No item-specific post returned; supplied pre-check and roadmap contain no Message Center post. This confirms absence from the available evidence, not absence from every tenant's Message center.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes permissions to start recording and transcription, not autonomous initiation.
claims.quote: Teams administrators can use meeting policies to control who can start recording and transcription

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Existing meeting options let organisers choose organisers and co-organisers, or organisers, co-organisers and presenters, unless a label or template enforces the choice.
claims.quote: Meeting organizer can choose who can record—Organizers and co-organizers or Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters—unless the setting is enforced by a label or template.

claims.claim: A meeting template can enforce who can record or allow the organiser to change that setting.
claims.quote: If not controlled by a sensitivity label, selects a setting of Organizers and co-organizers or Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters. Setting can be enforced or meeting organizer can be allowed to change.

claims.where: controls[4].governs; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Sensitivity labels can enforce who can record and transcribe.
claims.quote: To restrict transcription to organizers in meetings with sensitive information, use a meeting template or sensitivity label to enforce the Who can record and transcribe setting.

claims.claim: Current Learn documentation explicitly says there is no admin policy for Who can record.
claims.quote: Meeting recording can be disabled completely using a meeting policy, but there's no admin policy for Who can record.

claims.claim: Meeting recording is configured in Teams admin center under Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting recording.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies. Select an existing policy or create a new one. Turn the Meeting recording toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowCloudRecording $true enables recording for that meeting policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "Your Policy Name" -AllowCloudRecording $true

claims.claim: Both the organiser and recording initiator need recording permission under the existing recording policy.
claims.quote: Both the organizer and recording initiator need to have recording permissions to record the meeting or event.

claims.claim: Transcription is configured in Teams admin center under Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Transcription.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies. Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one. Toggle Transcription On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscription $true enables transcription for that meeting policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "Your Policy Name" -AllowTranscription $true

claims.claim: Transcription is both a per-organiser and per-user policy setting controlling whether transcription is allowed.
claims.quote: Transcription is both a per-organizer and per-user policy setting. For meetings and events to include transcripts, the organizer must have this setting turned on. The user who starts the recording or transcript must also have this setting turned on.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Organisers with Teams Premium can use meeting options to control who can record and transcribe.
claims.quote: Organizers with a Teams Premium license can use their meeting options to control who can record and transcribe.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; controls[3].note; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Meeting options in custom meeting templates require Teams Premium.
claims.quote: Meeting options in sensitivity labels and custom meeting templates require Teams Premium.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; controls[4].note; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Meeting options in sensitivity labels require Teams Premium.
claims.quote: Meeting options in sensitivity labels and custom meeting templates require Teams Premium.

claims.where: controls[].scope and notes; Why it matters
claims.claim: Meeting policies are user- or group-based, whereas label and template settings apply to the individual meetings using them.
claims.quote: Teams policies—including meeting policies—apply at the user or group level. Sensitivity label and template settings apply at the individual meeting level where those labels and templates are used.

claims.claim: The template control is in Teams admin center under Meetings > Meeting templates > Add > Recording & transcription > Who can record.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, expand Meetings and select Meeting templates. Select Add. ... Recording & transcription ... Who can record

claims.where: controls[3].api; controls[3].note; Governance controls: template row
claims.claim: Get-CsTeamsMeetingTemplateConfiguration retrieves custom templates and their meeting options, rather than setting those options.
claims.quote: Fetches the list of custom templates on the tenant. Each template object contains its list of meeting options, the name of the template, and its ID.

claims.claim: No setter for the custom meeting template options was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Set-CsTeamsMeetingTemplateConfiguration custom meeting template setter. Opened Get-CsTeamsMeetingTemplateConfiguration and create-custom-meeting-template; the reference says the configuration is read only and the search returned no template-options setter.

claims.claim: The label control is in the Purview Labels creation wizard under Protect Teams meetings and chats > Settings for Teams meetings and chats > Control who can record and transcribe.
claims.quote: On the Define the scope for this label page, make sure Files & other data assets, Emails, and Meetings are selected. ... On the Choose protection settings for types of items you selected page, select Protect Teams meetings and chats
claims.fix: Insert 'Define the scope for this label' between 'Create a label' and 'Choose protection settings for types of items you selected' in controls[4].ui.path and the rendered row. Its required selections are already correctly supplied in the note; the cited procedure includes this scope-selection page.

claims.claim: The label scope should include Files & other data assets, Emails and Meetings.
claims.quote: On the Define the scope for this label page, make sure Files & other data assets, Emails, and Meetings are selected.

claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity <label name> -TeamsWhoCanRecord <value> changes who can record for a meeting sensitivity label.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the sensitivity label that you want to modify. ... The TeamsWhoCanRecord parameter controls who can record Teams meetings. Valid values are: Organizer; Coorganizers; Presenters; $null (blank)

claims.claim: Set-Label runs in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Private meeting recordings are uploaded to the organiser's OneDrive.
claims.quote: It gets uploaded to the meeting organizer's OneDrive (private meetings) or SharePoint (channel meetings).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Channel meeting recordings are uploaded to SharePoint.
claims.quote: It gets uploaded to the meeting organizer's OneDrive (private meetings) or SharePoint (channel meetings).

claims.claim: Learn states that when organisers turn off Copilot in Teams meetings and events, recording and transcription are also turned off.
claims.quote: When organizers turn off Microsoft Copilot in Teams meetings and events, recording and transcription are also turned off.

claims.claim: Learn directs administrators to recording policies to prevent recording entirely and says that setting cannot be applied through templates or labels.
claims.quote: If you need to prevent meetings and events from being recorded entirely, you must use the recording policies in the Teams admin center. This setting applies to the people or groups that you specify, but can't be applied through a meeting template or sensitivity label.

claims.claim: A sensitivity label's Who can record and transcribe option does not take effect for a Meet Now meeting.
claims.quote: The following meeting options won't take effect for a Meet Now meeting: Who can record and transcribe

claims.claim: On with saved transcript required is an existing Copilot policy setting.
claims.quote: The only Copilot policy setting that you can enforce is On with saved transcript required.

claims.claim: Teams meeting policies support custom assignments as an alternative to changing the Global policy.
claims.quote: To apply changes to all users in your organization who don't have an existing policy assignment, use the Global policy. To exclude certain users from the global policy, create and assign a custom meeting policy.
